subject: SCIENCE
prompt: What force pulls objects toward the center of Earth?
explanation: Earth's gravity pulls objects down, toward the center of the planet.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: In a food chain, which organism is a producer?
explanation: Producers, such as grass and other plants, make their own food. Rabbits and hawks are consumers and mushrooms are decomposers.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Where is most of Earth's fresh water found?
explanation: Nearly all of Earth's water is salty ocean water. Most of the fresh water is frozen in glaciers and ice caps, and most of the rest is groundwater.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: The layer of gases (air) that surrounds Earth is called the ___.
explanation: The atmosphere is the layer of air around Earth. It interacts with the geosphere (rock), hydrosphere (water), and biosphere (living things).

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Why does the Sun look so much bigger and brighter than other stars?
choices: The Sun is the largest star in the universe
The Sun is much closer to Earth than other stars
Other stars do not give off light
Other stars shine only in winter
correctAnswer: The Sun is much closer to Earth than other stars
explanation: The Sun is a star of ordinary size. It appears larger and brighter because it is far closer to Earth than any other star.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Sugar is stirred into water until it can no longer be seen. The water tastes sweet. What happened to the sugar?
choices: It was destroyed and no longer exists at all
It broke apart into particles too small to see
It turned into water molecules and became water
It floated away into the air
correctAnswer: It broke apart into particles too small to see
explanation: Matter is made of particles too small to be seen. The sugar dissolved into tiny particles spread through the water; it is still there, which is why the water tastes sweet.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: A student mixes baking soda and vinegar in a cup. Bubbles of a gas form that was not there before. What does this show?
explanation: When some substances are mixed, new substances with different properties form. Baking soda and vinegar react to produce carbon dioxide gas, which makes the bubbles.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: A rabbit gets energy by eating grass. Where did the energy stored in the grass first come from?
explanation: Plants capture energy from sunlight to make their food. The energy in animals' food was once energy from the Sun.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Which are examples of the hydrosphere (water) changing the geosphere (rock and land)? Select all that apply.
choices: Ocean waves wearing away a cliff
A bird building a nest in a tree
Wind blowing clouds across the sky
correctAnswers: Ocean waves wearing away a cliff
explanation: Rivers and ocean waves are part of the hydrosphere, and they wear away rock and land, which are part of the geosphere.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Word bank: producers, consumers, decomposers. Fill in the blanks. Plants are ___ because they make their own food. Fungi and bacteria that break down dead organisms are ___.
explanation: Producers make their own food. Decomposers break down dead plants and animals and return materials to the soil.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Put these in order to show how energy flows through a food chain, starting with the original source of energy.
explanation: Energy from the Sun is captured by grass. The grasshopper eats the grass, the frog eats the grasshopper, and the hawk eats the frog.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: What causes day and night on Earth?
choices: Earth orbits the Sun once a year
The Sun orbits Earth once a day
The Moon blocks the Sun's light at night
explanation: Earth spins on its axis about once every 24 hours. The side facing the Sun has day and the side facing away has night.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: What mass of salt water should she find?
passage: A student poured 200 grams of water into a cup and measured out 15 grams of salt. She stirred the salt into the water until it could no longer be seen. Then she measured the mass of the salt water (not counting the cup).
explanation: Matter is conserved when substances are mixed. 200 grams of water plus 15 grams of salt make 215 grams of salt water, even though the salt can no longer be seen.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: A small seed grows into a large tree. Where does most of the material that makes up the tree's wood come from?
explanation: Plants get the materials they need for growth chiefly from air (carbon dioxide) and water. Sunlight provides the energy, but it is not matter, and only a small amount of material comes from soil.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Why was the shadow shortest at noon?
passage: On a sunny day a student measured the shadow of a 1-meter stick standing straight up. 9:00 a.m.: the shadow was 150 cm long and pointed west. 12:00 noon: the shadow was 40 cm long. 3:00 p.m.: the shadow was 150 cm long and pointed east.
choices: The Sun is closest to Earth at noon
The stick shrank in the heat
The Sun gives off less light at noon
The Sun was highest in the sky at noon
correctAnswer: The Sun was highest in the sky at noon
explanation: As Earth rotates, the Sun appears to move across the sky. Shadows are longest when the Sun is low (morning and afternoon) and shortest when the Sun is highest, around noon.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: A student has three unlabeled white powders: salt, sugar, and baking soda. Which test would best identify the baking soda?
choices: Adding vinegar to each powder to see which one bubbles
Looking at the color of each powder
Weighing one spoonful of each powder
Pouring each powder into a different cup
correctAnswer: Adding vinegar to each powder to see which one bubbles
explanation: Materials can be identified by their properties. Baking soda fizzes when vinegar is added, but salt and sugar do not. All three powders are white, so color does not help.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: If all the decomposers in a forest disappeared, what would most likely happen?
choices: Plants would grow faster than before, because nothing would be breaking them down
Animals would stop needing food, because there would be no decomposers to compete with
Dead plants and animals would pile up, and nutrients would not return to the soil
The forest would receive more sunlight
correctAnswer: Dead plants and animals would pile up, and nutrients would not return to the soil
explanation: Decomposers break down dead organisms and wastes and return materials to the soil for plants to use. Without them, matter would stop cycling through the ecosystem.

subject: SCIENCE
prompt: Why do we see different constellations in the night sky in summer than in winter?
choices: The stars themselves move around Earth once each year, so different stars are above us in each season
Earth orbits the Sun, so the night side of Earth faces different parts of space during the year
Summer constellations burn out before winter and new ones form each spring
correctAnswer: Earth orbits the Sun, so the night side of Earth faces different parts of space during the year
explanation: As Earth orbits the Sun over a year, the night side of Earth faces different directions in space, so different stars are visible in different seasons.
